youtube.title: What if you built the pyramids?
youtube.description:
Giza, around 2560 BC: you drag a 2.5-ton block on a wooden sledge while a guy pours water on the sand in front of it (wet sand cuts the pull in half). 🏜️🪨 Your gang is called "Friends of Khufu", your pay is bread and beer – and if you break an arm, a doctor splints it. One of the worst jobs in history… but not a job for slaves: the pyramid builders were paid in food, housed in a workers' town and buried in their own tombs next to the pyramid. (It wasn't exactly optional either – historians think most served a rotating labor duty.)
Would you sign up? A) Yes, for the beer B) Only as the water guy C) No way, too hot – Comment A, B or C 👇
Sources: Britannica, "Great Pyramid of Giza" (about 2.3 million blocks, ~2.5 t average); Mark Lehner / AERA (Ancient Egypt Research Associates), "The Lost City of the Pyramid Builders" (Heit el-Ghurab: bakeries, ~11 cattle and ~37 sheep and goats a day, analysis by Richard Redding); PBS NOVA, "Who Built the Pyramids?" (Lehner and Hawass: gangs like the "Friends of Khufu", workers' tombs, splinted fractures); A. Fall, D. Bonn et al., "Sliding Friction on Wet and Dry Sand", Physical Review Letters 112, 175502 (2014), University of Amsterdam; P. McGovern in Smithsonian Magazine (beer ration estimate up to 4–5 liters a day)
